title: restic, borg, casync and Xet
q3_concrete_actions: ADR-2 fixes chunk parameters at min 2 KiB / target 8 KiB / max 32 KiB — a row that exists in bench/results/raw/adr2-source-sweep.json — not Xet's 8/64/128, which Lattice has never measured. Justification: G1-8 p95 = 28,705 B (9x margin under the 262,144 target) with a structural worst case of 2 x 32 KiB = 65,536 B, versus exactly 262,144 B for a 128 KiB max; and it is the best row under 4 MiB bounded packs on django (0.64x git).

ADR-2 states the FastCDC normalisation level explicitly and reconciles it with the evidence: prototypes/chunkbench calls fastcdc::v2020::FastCDC::new, which defaults to Normalization::Level1, so the entire ADR-2 sweep was measured at NC-1. Either re-run the sweep through FastCDC::with_level(..., Normalization::Level2) or record NC-1 as the decision; borg 2's `fastcdc,19,23,21,2` may not be cited as evidence for a level Lattice did not measure.

ADR-2's central decision is the PACK FORMAT, not the chunk size: unique chunks are concatenated into a pack and compressed with a long window across chunk boundaries rather than per chunk. Measured on django (146,344 unique blobs, 3.066 GB raw, git gc --aggressive = 113.80 MB) with the prototype at HEAD: per-chunk zstd 2.83x-6.75x git across the sweep (all FAIL G1-9), long-window pack 0.51x-0.55x (all PASS), and the result is nearly independent of chunk size.

ADR-2 fixes 4 MiB independently decompressible seekable frames as the default compression unit and declares the frame size a named parameter of the pack format. Measured cost on django relative to an unbounded pack: 16 MiB frames 1.09-1.18x, 4 MiB 1.15-1.44x, 1 MiB 1.30-2.30x; at 4 MiB every parameter row lands between 0.63x and 0.75x git.

ADR-2 requires packs ordered by locality so successive versions of one path land adjacent, which is both the precondition for cross-chunk matching and what satisfies Xet's fragmentation rule (dedup runs of >=8 chunks or >=1 MB contiguous). ADR-2 carries the fragmentation policy explicitly because it now lands on G1-7 (max(switch p95 / 500ms, log p95 / 100ms) < 1.0).

The CAS interface stays get(chunk_hash) -> bytes and the chunker stays single, so cross-chunk compression is a storage-layer change invisible above the CAS and adds no eighth user-facing noun — but ADR-2 records 'one chunker for everything' as a bet, since borg 2 ships two chunker configurations (fastcdc,19,23,21,2 for content, fastcdc,15,19,17,2 for the metadata stream) and Hugging Face routes only .gitattributes-matched files through Xet.

ADR-3's store benchmark must report read amplification — bytes decompressed per chunk read — alongside store size, because that is exactly the cost restic, borg and casync paid per-chunk compression to avoid. At the recommended 4,330 B mean chunk, a 4 MiB frame is ~970x amplification and a 1 MiB frame ~240x, and it lands on G1-7's switch/log latency.

ADR-2 must not claim G1-9 on netty alone: the committed django artifact is the harder corpus and the one closer to Lattice's monorepo ambition. G1-9's restic leg (store/restic <= 1.25) must be measured or ADR-2 must state in writing that it is decorative — no restic baseline exists anywhere in bench/results/raw/.

ADR-2 states the per-repository chunker-seed tradeoff explicitly and records it as an accepted bet: Lattice wants stable cross-repository chunk identity for `ltx adopt` and native sync, which is precisely the watermarking-exposed configuration restic (random per-repo Rabin polynomial in `config`) and borg (per-repo buzhash XOR seed in the keyfile) engineered against. The mechanism is available — fastcdc::v2020::FastCDC::with_level_and_seed — so this is a decision, not an omission.

Lattice ships no global or cross-repository deduplication query without Xet-style HMAC protection of chunk hashes, matching the property 'raw chunk hashes are never transmitted from servers to clients'.

The redaction protocol defines chunk-level reference counting and a co-ownership resolution (re-materialise co-owners vs. refuse), and a gate must construct the case where a secret-bearing chunk is deduplicated into an innocent file.

Index budget is fixed at 50-100 bytes per chunk (borg measures ~51 and ~55 B/chunk marginal, documents 32+48 == 80 B on disk; Xet's MerkleDAG is ~0.5% of repo size), with borg's 2.1x rule applied to derive resident memory; chunkbench's 48 B/chunk constant is flagged as optimistic. At the recommended parameters django yields ~64,650 chunks/GB, so a 100 GB monorepo history is ~6.5 M chunks, ~520 MB index, ~1.1 GB resident — and the ephemeral autosnapshot tier's chunk-count and index-churn amplification must be measured before that tier ships.

G1-8's harness (harness/g1/g1_8_chunking.py, registered in harness/gates.toml but not yet written) must chunk real 50 MB files of all five declared types before ADR-2 fixes the max clamp; the existing edit-locality number comes from chunkbench running on 'the largest file available', a ~1-2 MB text file.

scripts/corpus/git_baseline.py's --commits N is fixed or deleted: it computes tip/oldest from rev-list -nN but then fetches the full branch history with no --depth and enumerates rev-list --objects --all, so 300- and 400-commit django runs measure the identical 34,907-commit object set. Any ADR-2 number must be regenerated from the committed prototype and re-committed in the same change.
uncomfortable_findings: G1-9's git-gc leg is unreachable by any chunk parameter under per-chunk compression. The gate is only reachable if the pack compresses ACROSS chunks — a pack-format decision ADR-3 explicitly left open and the spec does not currently make.

title: Dolt, Perforce and Subversion
q3_concrete_actions: ADR-5 (new): LTX directory nodes are prolly trees over the sorted entry-name space, with the chunker run over the NAME stream only (Dolt's keys-only refinement), so a same-length content-address update cannot move a boundary. Amends ADR-3, which fixes the pack format but leaves node shape open.

Property test `history_independence` in `crates/ltx-core`: over >=10,000 generated directory sets, the directory-tree root hash is byte-identical across shuffled insertion orders and across delete-then-reinsert.

New gate G1-13 'Directory write amplification' added to `harness/gates.toml` (harness `harness/g1/g1_13_dir_amplification.py`, hash-pinned in `harness/FREEZE.json`): p95 nodes rewritten when one entry is added to a 100,000-entry directory, HARD, target <=32.

Chunking policy becomes TWO independent path-scoped store attributes -- `chunk_target` (bytes) and `compress` (zstd|none) -- defaulted by content sniff, overridable per path. The `whole` mode is REJECTED and the rejection recorded in ADR-3, because a 50 MB single-chunk file persists 50 MB on a 1-byte edit and cannot pass G1-8's 262,144-byte target.

Every non-default `chunk_target` must still satisfy G1-8, which caps a coarse target at <=128 KiB; and G1-8's five file types must include an already-compressed binary drawn from the >=5 GiB G0-5 corpus so the constraint is actually exercised.

New gate G1-14 'Ingest throughput by content class' (SOFT) on the G0-5 binary corpus: `compress=none` must beat `compress=zstd` by >=1.3x on ingest wall-clock with dedup ratio within 2%; if it does not, the `compress` attribute is deleted and the 'all content through CDC' binding decision stands.

ADR-3 gains an index-residency clause and is re-measured at >=10^8 chunks reporting resident bytes per chunk, not only throughput and disk. Stated budget: <=512 MiB resident at 10^8 chunks (<=5.4 B/chunk), forcing a paged or per-pack-lazy pack index; failing it reopens redb for chunk content despite its measured 3.3x write amplification.

ADR-3 freezes address width at 32 bytes (BLAKE3-256) and explicitly REJECTS the 160-bit truncation, recording Git's SHA-256 transition rationale as the reason; chunk target size is decided in the same ADR revision since resident index bytes scale inversely with it.

LTX pack builder groups/sorts similar chunks before zstd as a HYPOTHESIS tested by G1-9 (storage honesty), not as an assumed win -- DoltHub reports only that chunks compress poorly in isolation and that grouping 'would result in much better compression'.

Workspace materialization scope is a declarative path ruleset on the `workspace` noun, modelled on Perforce stream paths, with subtractive `exclude` as the primary verb and SVN's ambient/sticky per-directory `--set-depth` semantics; G2-3 (HARD, zero nouns beyond seven) is the lint that keeps it noun-free.

G5-8 amended (or G5-9 added) to measure protocol round-trips against depth of divergence, not only 'initial transfer as a fraction of full store size': O(log n) rounds passes, O(n) degeneration on a wide chunk tree fails.

Autosnapshot thinning policy becomes path-scoped and declarative (shaped like Perforce `+Sn`), and G2-8 -- already requiring zero 'thinnings absent from op-log' -- is extended to assert per-path policies are honoured.

`ltx lock` is an advisory claim scoped to a named `remote`, recorded as an Ed25519-signed op-log entry; G2-3 is the enforcing gate, and help/error text may not introduce 'lock' or 'claim' as a user-facing noun.
`ltx sync` refuses to publish a change touching a path under another actor's live claim and names the holder, with an error satisfying G2-4 (recovery action plus causal category).
A `.lattice/lockable` pattern file (Perforce `typemap` / SVN `svn:needs-lock` shape) sets matching working files read-only on materialization.
Breaking a claim is itself a signed op-log entry, and `lock` / `break-lock` join G1-3's command alphabet so that undoing a lock break is exercised by the universal-undo gate.

`ltx lock` with no reachable remote must fail loudly ('advisory only, remote unreachable') rather than succeed locally; G5-6's >=10,000 randomized topologies gain a claim-collision class where two partitioned peers claiming the same path must converge to exactly one holder plus one logged loser.

G2-7's harness gains two named assertions: (a) deleting every lens definition and re-deriving yields a byte-identical checkpoint-DAG root hash AND an identical op-log root hash; (b) zero store writes occur during lens evaluation.
The lens engine takes a read-only store handle (`&dyn ReadStore`), so a write from lens evaluation is a compile error rather than a test failure.

ADR-1 (merge model) must state, before any G3 work, the encoding for publishing a checkpoint containing a live conflict object: either no lens may publish it and `ltx sync` refuses with a named recovery action, or the chosen textual encoding is entered in G3-4's lossy-edge ledger. Silence fails G3-1 (100% round-trip fidelity, HARD) and G3-3 (zero teammate anomalies, HARD).

Adopting a prolly-tree provenance index is a MEASURED decision against ADR-3's accepted redb choice, not an assumption: bench `prototypes/provindex`, judged on G5-4's 200 ms p95 for `ltx trace --agent --unreviewed --touching <path>` and on sync-delta size, with the winner and its number written into ADR-3.

Per-path READ authorization is written into the spec's non-goals so G6-4 (unacknowledged deviations, HARD) covers the omission, and partial materialization is documented as a convenience rather than a security boundary.
uncomfortable_findings: Lattice's own frozen gate G1-8 forbids the escape hatch this prior art says is necessary. G1-8 caps p95 new bytes persisted for a 1-byte edit in a 50 MB file at 262,144 bytes; Perforce's `+F` (full uncompressed file per revision) would persist 50 MB. Perforce can ship `+F` because it has no dedup obligation. Combined with DISAGREEMENTS Challenge 9 (CDC is the likeliest reason G1-9 fails against `git gc --aggressive` on source text), Lattice is squeezed from both sides: it cannot buy storage back with an unchunked mode, and CDC costs it storage on text. The only admissible relief is decoupling compression from chunking (skip zstd on incompressible content, keep CDC), which is a smaller win than the draft assumed.

ADR-3 is Accepted on evidence four orders of magnitude below the scale where the chosen option's known failure mode appears. The store benchmark used 40,000 chunks x 8 KiB (312.5 MiB). Dolt's NBS loads its whole chunk index into RAM at ~30 bytes/chunk (9 Mb for ~300K chunks); a 1 TiB Lattice depot at ADR-3's 8 KiB chunking is ~1.3x10^8 chunks (~4 GB resident) and ~2.7x10^8 at a 4 KiB target (~8 GB). Resident index bytes were never measured. The custom-pack option may be unviable for a local-first tool on a laptop, and the ADR's confidence is not yet earned.

Copying Dolt's 20-byte (160-bit) address would be a security regression, and refusing it makes the index problem worse. Dolt truncates SHA-512 to 20 bytes for a single-writer database of the operator's own rows. Lattice ingests third-party content, syncs peer-to-peer, and signs provenance attestations over hashes, so a collision forges attribution. Git left 160-bit hashes deliberately ('SHA-1 is still weak'; a broken hash means 'we could not trust that a given hash value represented the known good version of content'). Keeping 32 bytes is correct and costs ~+40% per Dolt-shaped index entry -- compounding the residency finding above rather than relieving it.

'Merges never block' is undercut by the closest architectural cousin, which built exactly Lattice's conflict model and still blocks. Dolt stores conflicts by primary key in a separate prolly tree holding into/from/ancestor, and nonetheless: 'Merges with schema conflicts will prevent the merge from completing'; 'Dolt will not allow you to commit transactions that have merge conflicts, and will automatically rollback any transaction with merge conflicts'; 'Constraint violations from merge detected, cannot commit transaction.' Storing conflicts as objects buys queryability, not an unblocked write path, because downstream consumers need a well-defined state.

Git has no representation for a committed conflict, and this is unresolved on the critical path. A lens rendering a Lattice checkpoint containing a live conflict object must either refuse to publish (merges block, later and less legibly) or inline textual conflict markers (losing structured both-sides+base). The Git bridge ships BEFORE the semantic and agent layers, and two HARD gates -- G3-1 (100% round-trip fidelity) and G3-3 (zero anomalies for Git-only teammates) -- both bite on whichever answer ADR-1 chooses.

Lattice has no exclusive-locking story at all -- `lock` does not appear in the spec -- and structural merge is not a substitute: nothing in tree-sitter merges two .psd or .uasset files. Every prior system concluded locking is mandatory for un-mergeable binaries (Perforce `+l`/typemap, SVN `svn lock`/`svn:needs-lock`, Git LFS bolted it on). Correction to the draft: the Git LFS proposal does NOT say atomicity 'requires a central server'; it says its aim is 'to discourage (we can never prevent) parallel editing of binary files', with the server as the component that 'must atomically check/set'. The corrected evidence is stronger -- even centralized locks are advisory -- so any Lattice lock can only ever be advisory and remote-scoped, and adding it forces a locking verb into a vocabulary G2-3 polices at target 0.

Lattice cannot offer the per-path READ authorization that both Perforce and SVN provide, because full content-addressed history reaches every peer. Redaction is a post-hoc remedy for leaked secrets, not access control; partial materialization is a convenience, not a boundary. Any team needing 'this directory must never reach that contractor's clone' is unserved, and the omission is currently undocumented, which is itself a G6-4 exposure.

Ecosystem beat capability for SVN, and Lattice has de-scoped the ecosystem. SVN's defeat was sealed by GitHub, not by mergeinfo (Git 93.87% vs SVN 5.18%, Stack Overflow 2022, n=71,379). With hosting, review and CI out of scope and published history a lens-generated Git projection, provenance, conflict objects and the op-log are exactly what a teammate reviewing on GitHub cannot see. G3-6 measures that lenses generate the publishes; nothing measures whether the differentiator is visible to anyone outside the repo.

Performance targets are likely unrealistic, and the calibration is now sourced precisely. DoltHub: 'Four years ago DoltDB was about 15x slower than MySQL' (Dec 2024); 1.16x immediately before the last optimization round; 0.99 mean multiple at parity (Dec 2025) -- roughly five years, on a problem with primary keys to lean on. DoltHub also names the mechanism Lattice shares: Dolt 'misses out on taking as much advantage of write buffering and write optimized data structures like LSMTs ... partly because of its requirement to materialize the full tree and realize a content address for it so often.' Lattice's continuous auto-snapshotting hits that path far more often than Git does. G1-6's 250 ms p95 for `ltx save` is the most exposed gate; 2-5x slower than Git on write-heavy workloads is the realistic v1 expectation.

Write amplification travels with fan-out, and every derived index is a multiplier on `ltx save`. DoltHub rejected columnar storage because inserting one row into a 256-column table would 'update at least 256 independent places on disk'. Any Lattice change that fans across checkpoint DAG, op-log, provenance index, semantic index and lens caches inherits this. This specifically undercuts the appealing recommendation to build a prolly-tree provenance index: ADR-3 has already Accepted redb for the provenance index, and replacing it must be a measured decision (G5-4's 200 ms p95, sync-delta size), not an assumption.

The seven-noun bet has no support in this prior art. Perforce exposes depot, stream, client, changelist, label, branch spec, typemap, protections, shelf and job, and dominates its market; SVN exposed roughly four and lost. Noun count is uncorrelated with adoption in this sample. Simplicity is a retention property, not an acquisition one -- and the locking gap already forces a new verb into the vocabulary that G2-3 polices at target 0.

Even the centralized answer to per-workspace state does not scale for free, which raises the bar for Lattice's materialization ruleset. Perforce's own docs concede that with 'many clients syncing a large number of files at the same time, the central [db.have] table is subject to contention', and ship partitioned `db.have.pt` tables per client to escape it. Lattice has no server to hold this state at all and must pay in round-trips -- yet G5-8 measures only 'initial transfer as a fraction of full store size', a bytes-only metric that cannot see O(n) round-trip degeneration on a wide chunk tree.

title: gitoxide and libgit2
q3_concrete_actions: ADR-BRIDGE-LIC (proposed, blocking): Lattice does not link libgit2. Rationale recorded as the one-way GPLv2 patch valve (COPYING: GPL restrictions 'cover modification of the file'), explicitly NOT as licence incompatibility, since Vicent Martí closed libgit2 #567 confirming the linking exception is Apache-2.0 compatible.

Add `[bans] deny = [{ name = "libgit2-sys" }, { name = "git2" }]` to `deny.toml` plus a CI assertion both entries are present — a ban, not a licence rule. Verified necessary: the published libgit2-sys-0.18.8+1.9.7.crate declares `MIT OR Apache-2.0` on crates.io while vendoring `libgit2/COPYING` (GPLv2) and 202 `.c` files its build script compiles, so `cargo deny licenses` passes it silently.

ADR-BRIDGE-DEPS (proposed): read-path-only dependency on gix-hash, gix-actor, gix-date, gix-validate, gix-object, gix-pack, gix-odb, gix-ref, gix-config, gix-config-value, gix-url, gix-refspec, gix-glob, gix-ignore, gix-pathspec, gix-discover, gix-index (read), gix-packetline, gix-transport, gix-protocol (fetch + ls-refs only), gix-credentials — with the ADR recording that none is Production Grade: six are Stabilization Candidates and fifteen are Initial Development.

gix-attributes downgraded from unconditional buy to CONDITIONAL, pending review of RUSTSEC-2024-0359 (unsound `&str` from non-UTF-8 bytes leaked to kstring/serde) and of crate-status.md's unchecked 'attributes stack for matching paths to their attributes'.

Do NOT depend on gix-worktree-state or gix-status (imports Git's checkout model plus CVE-2024-35186 and CVE-2025-22620 classes), gix-merge/gix-diff for user-visible semantics (gix-diff `[ ] diff-heuristics match Git perfectly`; gix-merge's own status: 'too insane now'), or gix-reftable (empty). Exclude gix-filter on MODEL grounds (Lattice runs no clean/smudge filters) — explicitly not on 'every box unchecked', which is false.

ADR-BRIDGE-XPORT: Lattice implements its own send-pack/receive-pack client — report-status, sideband-64k, delete-refs, push-options, atomic pushes, object-format negotiation — because gix-protocol leaves all four checkboxes unchecked and gitoxide #306 is closed not-planned. Budgeted as the largest single bridge item.

ADR-BRIDGE-PACK: Lattice implements its own delta search, or records a measured, numeric accepted wire cost. Justification sharpened: gix-pack's `Entry::from_data` unconditionally yields `Kind::Base(obj.kind)` and the deltifying `from_pack_entry` path requires an existing local Git pack, which Lattice (CDC chunk store) never has — so every pushed object takes from_data, not merely the lens-generated ones.

ADR-BRIDGE-SHADOW: `ltx-gitcompat` stores each IMPORTED Git object as its exact byte buffer keyed by SHA-1, chunked into the CDC store; re-emission of an unmodified imported object is a buffer copy. Scope explicitly limited in the ADR to the adopt-and-return path — lens-generated objects have no stored bytes and must be serialized from the typed model.

ADR-BRIDGE-HASH: use `sha1-checked` pinned to the stable 0.10 line (0.11.0-rc.0 is a pre-release) and error on `CollisionResult::Collision`, matching C Git since 2.13.0; pin `gix-features >= 0.41.0` to exclude CVE-2025-31130.

ADR-BRIDGE-ISO: exactly one workspace crate, `ltx-gitcompat`, may name a `gix-*` type; CI fails on any `gix` import outside `ltx-gitcompat/`. Bounds the thirteen breaking gix minor bumps between Oct 2025 and Aug 2026 to one crate.

Adversarial-tree corpus for the bridge gate covering `..`, `.git` case variants, NTFS 8.3 short names, `.git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION`, trailing dots/spaces and symlinked parents; every path write funnels through one validated join. EXTENDED: the corpus must also assert resulting file modes and symlink targets, because RUSTSEC-2025-0001 was a permissions bug (0777 via a strategy not subject to umask) that a path-only corpus cannot catch.

Gate G-BRIDGE-FIDELITY replaces the ≥1000-cycles × ≥10-repos gate with: (a) ≥1000 distinct repositories at one cycle each, scored on object-shape coverage rather than repo count; (b) a pathological corpus seeded from gitoxide #1542 (tagger with no timestamp), #1922 (email trailing space trimmed at parse time), #1923 (`+051800` offset), #2177 (unmaterializable CommitRef) — and explicitly NOT #2491, which is an error-message complaint, not a fidelity defect; (c) the corpus must exercise Lattice's serializer, not only the shadow store.

Standing rule for the bridge: any build-vs-buy decision citing a gitoxide `crate-status.md` checkbox must be re-verified against the crate source at pin time, because the file demonstrably lags reality (gix-filter and signed-commit creation both shipped while still marked unchecked).
uncomfortable_findings: The byte-faithful shadow store does NOT make round-trip fidelity structural for the path that matters. It only holds objects Lattice imported. Lattice's binding decision is that Git-facing history is LENS-GENERATED — those commits and trees never existed in Git, so no stored byte buffer exists and they must be serialized from Lattice's typed model, i.e. exactly the `Commit::write_to` path that re-encodes a parsed signature through a date formatter and loses `+051800`. Fidelity is an invariant only for adopt-then-push-back-unchanged; for the main push path it remains statistical. The draft's headline Q3 claim is scoped wrong.

The claim that a gix `CommitRef` decode/encode cycle is 'a byte copy' is false, and gitoxide issue #2177 — which the draft itself cites — is literally titled 'The CommitRef ... cannot be materialized or round-tripped'. `CommitRef::write_to` also re-emits tree/parent via parsed ObjectIds and re-emits `encoding` at a fixed position. Any Lattice design that leans on a borrowed-view round-trip as its fidelity mechanism inherits a defect gitoxide has already shipped.

The byte-faithful shadow store doubles adopt-time storage: every imported Git object is held twice, as its zlib-framed Git byte buffer and as Lattice content, and the two chunk differently so CDC dedup across them is partial at best. Adopting a monorepo costs roughly 2x on disk — directly against pillar (3) of Lattice's own thesis, that Git's storage chokes on monorepos.

gitoxide's `crate-status.md` — the primary evidence base for Lattice's entire build-vs-buy decision — is demonstrably stale. It marks gix-filter's clean/smudge/process bases unchecked while `gix-filter/src/lib.rs` ships Pipeline, driver, eol, ident and worktree encoding, and it marks 'create signed commits and tags' unchecked while the August 2026 report announces OpenPGP, X.509 and SSH signing and verification 'all supported and tested'. A dependency decision built on checkbox archaeology is built on sand.

Every crate in Lattice's proposed read-path buy list is pre-1.0 and NONE is Production Grade. gitoxide's own README places only gix-lock and gix-tempfile in the Production tiers; six of the buy list are Stabilization Candidates and fifteen — including gix-object, gix-pack, gix-odb, gix-protocol, gix-transport and gix-index — are 'Initial Development'. The draft's rationale that these are the crates covered by the on-disk-format promise is also wrong for gix-transport, gix-protocol, gix-credentials and gix-url, which are wire/config crates covered by no promise at all.

The bought fetch path carries a hang documented by the maintainer. gitoxide's SHORTCOMINGS.md: 'Fetches using protocol V1 and stateful connections, i.e. ssh, git, file, may hang.' `ltx sync` over SSH is precisely that shape. The same file warns that gix-pack's mmap use 'squelch[es] IO errors' and that gix-url 'might be more restrictive than what Git allows'.
